title: Count material, state the boundary
hook: A heavier reusable container and light replacements accumulate material differently.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Compare cumulative material amounts while stating what the account excludes.

misconception: A material-mass comparison alone proves the lower environmental impact.
objective: Compare cumulative material amounts while stating what the account excludes.

claims.text: A toy reusable container starts at 200g and uses 2g of replacement material/use. Single-use replacements each use 20g. Scaled model; toy masses; material only; no lifecycle claim.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Uses=10, A=220g and B=200g. The geometry pictures follow the declared dimension relationships; other stage pictures are scaled to the larger displayed comparison and icons are not literal item counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",200,["*",2,"x"]]; B=["*",20,"x"]; x denotes Uses. At x=10, A=220, B=200; recall at x=13: B=260. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.

claims.text: Include the starting material and the repeated additions within the chosen boundary. This toy mass account excludes energy, cleaning, transport and disposal; lower mass here does not establish a lower environmental impact.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["+",200,["*",2,"x"]]; B=["*",20,"x"]; x denotes Uses. At x=10, A=220, B=200; recall at x=13: B=260. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits.

claims.text: A toy reusable container starts at 200g and uses 2g of replacement material/use. Single-use replacements each use 20g. Change only Uses to 13. What is B (Replaced) now? Correct: 260g. Use B's stated rule with Uses=13: it gives 260g. Include the starting material and the repeated additions within the chosen boundary. This toy mass account excludes energy, cleaning, transport and disposal; lower mass here does not establish a lower environmental impact.

recall.question: A toy reusable container starts at 200g and uses 2g of replacement material/use. Single-use replacements each use 20g. Change only Uses to 13. What is B (Replaced) now?
recall.why: Use B's stated rule with Uses=13: it gives 260g. Include the starting material and the repeated additions within the chosen boundary. This toy mass account excludes energy, cleaning, transport and disposal; lower mass here does not establish a lower environmental impact.

safety.assumptions: A toy reusable container starts at 200g and uses 2g of replacement material/use. Single-use replacements each use 20g.
safety.excluded: No chemical mixtures, medical advice, wiring, safety-device bypass, actual tariffs, financial recommendations, temperature, food-storage or food-safety instructions. All energy powers, durations and tariffs are illustrative.
